data.narrative:
Tekever, a Series C-stage defense and security company that has raised $631M+ to date, is evaluated against a peer universe of 10 comparables: 2 public companies (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and 8 private firms including Castelion, Stark Defence, Neros, Anduril Industries, and Helsing.

Two valuation methods were triangulated. The stage-progression method, applying a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C advancement to the $631M raised proxy, implies a valuation of $1.1B. The peer-median method anchors on three same-sector, same-stage comparables—Castelion ($13.0B), Stark Defence ($4.0B), and Neros ($2.5B)—yielding a median of $4.0B and a range of $2.5B to $13.0B. The divergence between methods reflects material dispersion in recent Defense & Security valuations at this stage.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $912M (low) to $4.6B (high), with a median of $2.5B. The $3.7B spread underscores significant uncertainty around Tekever's positioning relative to peers. Key variables include revenue scale relative to the comparable set, customer concentration and contract durability in defense markets, and whether the company occupies a performance tier closer to Neros or Castelion within the peer band. Stage and sector fundamentals support the lower-to-mid range absent differentiation evidence.
